answer: When a newcomer joins the market, a rising identity bond requires locking saffron into an on-chain oasis before signing orders. During every comet, an auditor measures mutual information across active agents' response latencies and trade vectors; if $m$ identities exceed the correlation threshold, the $m$-th correlated identity must lock $80 \cdot 3^{m-1}$ saffron into the oasis for that comet. A lone newcomer locks 80 saffron per comet, while one operator running $n$ clones from shared infrastructure must lock $40(3^n - 1)$ saffron per comet or run $n$ unlinked stacks.
